AM14F-01.bounds: Not an interval item; the only forced constraint is membership. The answer is a VALUE OF f, and f's listed range is {5,7,13,2}. Option 3 is not in the range of f, so it dies to that observation alone. 2 = f(4), 7 = f(2), 13 = f(3) are all legal outputs of f at an in-domain input, so all three survive. No ordering or magnitude bound exists.
issues: Inline function values (item 5 of the brief): reads unambiguously as plain text. Every value is individually labelled f(n)= / g(n)=, the two lists are separated by 'and', 'defined only for the inputs shown' fixes the domain, and no value is multi-digit-with-thousands so the comma separators cannot be misread. No table needed.
Positive, not a defect: all four options appear somewhere in the stem's value lists, so there is no odd-one-out tell of the 'three options are table values, one is invented' kind.
f(2)=7 and g(2)=7 share a value; this makes 7 reachable by two wrong routes rather than one, which is harmless here but means the '7' distractor does not uniquely diagnose order reversal.

AM14G-03.bounds: The 30 cm side is a chord, so the diameter exceeds 30 strictly => area > pi(15^2) = 706.9. The diagonal is less than the sum of the sides (triangle inequality), so diameter < 46 => area < pi(23^2) = 1661.9. Feasible band (706.9, 1661.9). Survivors: 804, 908, 1511. 480 fails: it is less than the area of the rectangle the circle strictly contains.
issues: 480 sits EXACTLY on the part-not-exceeding-whole bound: it is the area of the inscribed rectangle (16 x 30), and the circle's area is strictly greater than that by containment. It is therefore free to eliminate with one trivial multiplication and no geometry. Mitigating: the elimination does NOT leak the tested insight (diagonal = diameter), and 3 options remain, so this is a weak distractor rather than a giveaway. Flagged, not spent.

1511 survives only a loose bound; it implies a diagonal of 43.9 against a true 34, i.e. a nearly degenerate rectangle, but recognising that requires doing the arithmetic, so it is counted as surviving.

Feasible band (6, 12). Survivors: 6.9, 8.5, 10.4. 13.4 fails: it exceeds the hypotenuse 12, i.e. exceeds the side it is dropped inside, and dies to leg-less-than-hypotenuse with no computation.
issues: The bound values 6 and 12 are not themselves options, so nothing sits on a bound.

6.9 = 12/sqrt(3) is also the CIRCUMRADIUS of this triangle. That is a real quantity of the figure, but the stem says 'an altitude' with no ambiguity, so it is not a defensible reading - only a second, more flattering story for why a student lands there.
No arithmetic run (diffs 1.6, 1.9, 3.0), no 2:1 pair, no duplicates. Key is in slot 3 of 4.

issues: 204 is the lateral area alone, a proper PART of the requested total, so it also sits exactly on the total-exceeds-lateral bound. Unlike AM14G-03's 480 this elimination is NOT free - reaching 204.2 requires the Pythagorean step that is the item's actual work - so it is flagged for shape, not for cheapness. It is separately dead to the l > h monotonicity bound above, which is cheap; either way it does not survive.
The stem's explicit 'including its circular base' forecloses the one reading under which 204 would be correct. That phrase is load-bearing and must not be edited out.
